quotes.text: A code app is a power app that you write in code instead of dragging and dropping.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Simplest one-line definition of code apps.

quotes.text: Canvas apps are pre-furnished rooms. You walk in the furniture is already there. You just rearrange things to your liking. Code apps are empty rooms where you bring your own furniture.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable analogy contrasting canvas apps and code apps.

quotes.text: The SDK handles the complexity of authentication, data serialization and error handling. You focus on what you want to do.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains the role of the Power Apps SDK in one sentence.

quotes.text: Code apps are subject to the same governance as canvas apps. They appear in solutions. They can be deployed through pipelines. They inherit environment policies.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Counters the myth that code apps escape governance.

quotes.text: code apps aren't a separate platform. They're not a new tool you have to learn from scratch.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the key insight that code apps build on the existing platform.

What the Power Apps SDK does
How it all fits together and next steps

takeaways: Power Apps code apps are written in JavaScript, TypeScript and React in VS Code but still run inside Power Apps with hosting and authentication handled by the platform.
The Power Apps SDK generates typed model and service files for Dataverse, SharePoint and other connectors, and DLP and environment policies still apply.
Code apps need a Power Apps Premium license and must be enabled per environment by an admin; they extend canvas apps rather than replace them.
hook: Hit the limits of the drag-and-drop canvas? This episode explains Power Apps code apps in plain English for pro developers and makers, covering how they differ from canvas apps, how the SDK connects your React code to Power Platform data, and how governance and licensing work.
